subject: Production: 5xx/429 surge — retransmit flood from client SDK (needs exec attention)
messages:
From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@finops.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyanka Shah <pri@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike — logs attached

Hi Neha,

We're seeing a sudden surge of 5xx/429 responses from Redwood between 08:50–09:05 PDT across multiple services. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~8% and latency increased sharply. Customers downstream are reporting timeouts and retries.

We've attached a small sample of our client-side metrics and connection traces (perf_logs_20260820.zip). Quick note from our engineering team: they're using Acme's internal wrapper around your JS SDK (v1.4.0) with retries configured to 5 attempts and a fixed 200ms retry delay — no jitter. Suspect their client is amplifying load when the service started returning transient 5xxs.

Can your team confirm if there was any capacity issue or rollout on your side? This is causing significant impact for Acme's production customers.

Thanks,
Tom
Ops Lead — FinOps (on behalf of Acme Analytics)
Attachment: perf_logs_20260820.zip (approx 58 KB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@finops.io>
Cc: Priyanka Shah <pri@acme-analytics.com>; Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>; Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike — logs attached

Tom — thank you for the quick heads-up and the logs. I've looped in Monica (Customer Reliability) and Rishi (Engineering leadership).

Immediate plan:
- Monica will validate whether the spike originated from our routing/serving layer or if it looks client-amplified.
- If client-side retransmits are the primary driver, we can: (a) advise a config change on their SDK, (b) apply a temporary token-level rate cap on our side to stabilize latency, and (c) consider a one-time account credit to offset the impact.
- We’ll set up a short bridge if useful — are you available at 10:00 PDT?

Priyanka — can you confirm whether you can alter the SDK retry settings quickly? If not, we’ll proceed with server-side protections while we coordinate a longer fix.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference | https://redwood.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>; Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>; Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@finops.io>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike — logs attached

On Thu, Aug 20, 2026 at 9:30 AM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Tom — thank you for the quick heads-up and the logs.

I've pulled the sample traces (thanks for sending). Quick summary of what I see:
- Initial source: an upstream service experienced a transient CPU pressure causing ~30s tail latency (this aligns with internal infra alerts at 08:47).
- Amplification: Acme's SDK wrapper appears to retry aggressively (max_retries=5, retry_delay=200ms, no jitter). When the first 5xx returned, the client issued near-immediate retries across many parallel requests, which turned an isolated transient into a sustained higher QPS and more 5xx/429s.
- Evidence: timestamped request IDs in your traces show identical request payloads retransmitted 3–5x within a 1s window for many keys.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (ordered):
1) Temporary server-side token throttling for the affected Acme project to keep overall P99 latency reasonable (we can do a soft cap at present request rate).
2) Advise Acme to change their SDK config to an exponential backoff with jitter (recommended initial backoff 200ms +/- jitter, multiplier 2, max_retries 2).
3) We will prepare a hotfix in our SDK that changes defaults to safer retries (INF-7892).

Attachments: acme_sdk_config_snapshot.txt (their config snippet), INF-7892-client-retry-analysis.pdf (analysis + recommended server-side knobs).

I'll remain on the bridge if you spin one up.

—Monica
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: acme_sdk_config_snapshot.txt; INF-7892-client-retry-analysis.pdf
From: Priyanka Shah <pri@acme-analytics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>; Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike — logs attached

Neha / Monica — thanks for the quick analysis. We do have the wrapper around your SDK deployed across multiple teams and cannot push changes to every service instantly; many are in separate CD pipelines. We can change the wrapper today for a canary group but full rollout will take several hours.

Please proceed with the temporary server-side cap — we need system stability first. Also, we’d like to request a credit for the impact window (08:45–10:15 PDT) while you investigate.

Priyanka
VP, Platform Engineering — Acme Analytics
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>; Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@finops.io>; Priyanka Shah <pri@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: credit request + temporary throttle for Acme (INF-7892)

Rishi / Laura — heads-up and request for quick decision: Acme is asking for a one-time credit for the impact window while we stabilize their traffic. Monica confirms the root cause is client retransmit amplification due to their SDK defaults (INF-7892). Acme cannot roll out the wrapper update instantly.

Recommended actions:
- Approve a one-time credit of up to 20% of their August usage (pro-rated for the 1.5-hour window) to preserve the relationship.
- Approve immediate temporary rate cap on their project token (soft throttle) until Acme can roll their canary.
- Greenlight SDK defaults change and schedule the SDK patch release (Engineering to own INF-7892).

If you’re OK, I’ll notify Priyanka and implement the throttle immediately.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>; Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@finops.io>; Priyanka Shah <pri@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: credit request + temporary throttle for Acme (INF-7892)

Thanks Neha — approved.
- Approve 20% one-time credit for the impact window (finance to process).
- Monica: please apply a soft token-level request cap for Acme immediately and monitor P50/P99.
- Engineering (me): INF-7892 is a priority; change SDK default retry behavior to exponential backoff with jitter and reduce default max_retries. Schedule release by EOW and include a migration note.
- Postmortem required within 5 business days. Laura, please coordinate customer communications and ensure the credit is processed.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Reliability & Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference

On Thu, Aug 20, 2026 at 1:45 PM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Rishi / Laura — heads-up and request for quick decision: Acme is asking for a one-time credit...

---
Summary of actions taken:
- Temporary soft throttle applied to Acme project token at 14:10 PDT.
- Customer canary patch guidance provided; Acme began canary rollout at ~15:35 PDT.
- One-time credit approved (20%) and queued with Finance.
- INF-7892 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7892

Next steps: detailed postmortem and SDK default change release notes.
